evals.prompt: I have one dirty Git worktree with a bug fix, some import reordering, and a manual CHANGELOG.md edit. I want a preview first, then exact split commits without using interactive patch prompts.
evals.expected_output: Builds a preview split plan, distinguishes trivial import-only work, keeps the changelog hunk with the right logical commit, and uses noninteractive precise-staging guidance instead of assuming TTY patch mode.
expectations: The plan previews numbered commits before mutation
The workflow assigns every intended hunk to exactly one commit
The answer uses patch-file or pathspec-file Git flows instead of only `git add -p`
The changelog edit stays with the commit it describes rather than becoming a catch-all docs commit

evals.prompt: Commit only these Git paths, including one filename with spaces, and leave the rest of the dirty repo untouched. Use a temp message file and tell me what validation you would run.
evals.expected_output: Uses pathspec-from-file style staging for awkward filenames, keeps unrelated work untouched, commits via a message file, and proposes a narrow validation gate.
expectations: The workflow uses a NUL-safe path list or equivalent for weird filenames
The answer does not sweep unrelated dirty files into the commit
The commit command uses `git commit -F "$msgfile"`
The answer proposes focused validation instead of defaulting to a full-repo suite

evals.prompt: I already made one mixed Git commit by mistake. Split the last commit into honest commits, preserve new-file partial staging, and recover cleanly if I over-stage during the rewrite.
evals.expected_output: Uses the reset-and-restage split recipe, preserves partial new-file staging with `git add -N`, and includes an exact recovery path for over-staging.
expectations: The workflow uses `git reset -N HEAD^` or an equivalent split-last-commit recipe
The answer keeps new files visible to partial staging
The answer includes reverse-apply or another exact over-staging recovery method
The final flow still commits from a message file

evals.prompt: This repo is GitButler-managed. I need to commit only two exact hunks from one file, then reword the commit from a temp message file, and I want the plan to survive ID churn after each mutation.
evals.expected_output: Uses `but` JSON inspection, commits specific change IDs, treats post-mutation JSON as source of truth, and handles rewording without dropping the message-file workflow.
expectations: The workflow starts from `but status --json` and `but diff --json`
The answer commits exact change IDs rather than falling back to raw Git writes
The answer refreshes IDs after each mutation
The reword flow preserves a temp-message-file workflow directly or via file-to-string handoff

evals.prompt: Figure out whether this repo wants manual changelog edits or release-note fragments before committing. If only heavy validation exists, do not guess; make me approve the tradeoff.
evals.expected_output: Detects changelog system type, applies the correct commit grouping rule, and escalates heavy or ambiguous validation with clarify instead of silently choosing.
expectations: The workflow checks repo docs or release files to distinguish manual changelogs from fragment systems
The answer avoids hand-editing generated changelogs when automation owns them
The answer keeps release-note edits with the change they describe
The answer asks for approval when validation cost or scope is unclear
